PostHog AI pricing
Contents
Each time you interact with an AI-powered feature – whether you're asking PostHog AI to write SQL, summarize data, or analyze sessions – credits are spent based on the resources required to complete your request.
This means you pay for what you use.
There’s no fixed subscription and every organization gets a monthly free tier worth $5 (500 AI credits) to explore PostHog AI's features.
For reference, 100 AI credits = $1 .
We apply a simple, consistent 20% markup over the underlying LLM provider’s cost. So 1 PostHog AI credit corresponds to $0.008333 of raw inference.

What consumes AI credits
AI credits are consumed whenever PostHog performs intelligent work for you. You’ll spot these features by the icon or when using the in-app chat.
Examples include:
* Searching for session recordings in natural language
* Summarizing experiment results
* Writing or debugging SQL with AI
* Summarizing survey responses
* AI summaries in insight and dashboard subscriptions
* Prompt subscriptions
What doesn't consume AI credits
Getting help on how to use PostHog (i.e., asking questions about our docs) does not use AI credits.
AI features in beta are also free to use.
How AI credit usage works
AI credits are based on the underlying token costs , which reflect the effort required to complete your request.
* Simple queries like "What were my daily active users in October?" use very few tokens, and therefore very few credits.
* More complex tasks like analyzing hundreds of session recordings or rewriting a SQL query multiple times use more tokens and consume more credits.
* PostHog automatically selects the most efficient model for each AI feature.
Track your AI credit usage
Stay on top of your AI credit spend in real time:
Control your AI credit spend
You’re always in control of your AI credit usage:
* Real-time tracking: See costs as you go
* Custom billing limit: Set hard caps to prevent overspending
* Default billing limit: PostHog sets a default $150 billing limit so you don't accidentally rack up costs without a ceiling
* Usage alerts: Get notified when you hit key thresholds
When you hit your credit limit, AI features pause until your credits reset at the next billing period. For subscriptions:
* Prompt subscriptions are paused entirely and automatically resume when credits are available.
* Insight and dashboard subscriptions with AI summaries continue to deliver on schedule, but without the AI-generated summary.

evidence.title: PostHog vs Mixpanel in-depth tool comparison
evidence.snippet:
Price comparison
PostHog and Mixpanel both charge based on the number of events ingested, however:
* Want an all-in-one developer platform that goes beyond analytics with error tracking , LLM observability , feature flags , and transparent pricing + a generous free tier to get you started? Go with PostHog .
* Prefer a polished UI optimized for product managers and growth teams, with strong warehouse-native analytics? Mixpanel is a solid choice.
* Mixpanel – Purpose-built for non-technical users with a polished interface, metric trees for aligning teams on goals, and strong collaboration features.
For teams building AI products
* PostHog – Native LLM observability for tracking AI usage, model performance, token costs, and debugging LLM interactions. Mixpanel doesn't offer AI observability.
* PostHog – A single platform that scales from MVP to growth stage without rebuilding your stack. The generous free tier means you won't outgrow it quickly. Startups can also qualify for $50k in free credits .
* | Free usage per month
* Product analytics | 1 million events
* Session replay | 5,000 recordings
Consider keeping Mixpanel if your team is heavily invested in Mixpanel's metric trees for goal alignment, you prefer their polished UI for non-technical users, or you're using warehouse-native analytics with Mixpanel sitting directly on your data warehouse. How much does Mixpanel cost?
Mixpanel has three tiers:
1. Free: 1M events/month, core analytics, limited features
2. Growth: Starts ~$28/month per 10k events after, scales with volume
3. Enterprise: Custom pricing, includes experiments, advanced features
Add-ons like Group Analytics, Data Pipelines, and Experiments are separately priced. Session Replay is included but limited by recording count.
Mixpanel added AI-powered replay summaries and heatmap comparison mode in late 2025. PostHog's free tier includes 5,000 replays/month; Mixpanel's replay limits depend on your plan. Can I use PostHog and Mixpanel together?
Yes, though most teams find it redundant. If you're migrating gradually, you can run both in parallel.
The generous free tier covers most startup needs, and the PostHog for Startups program offers $50k in additional credits. More importantly, you get a single platform that scales from MVP to growth stage without needing to add tools as you grow.
PostHog can replace Google Analytics for many use cases – our marketing team uses PostHog , for example. You can also integrate PostHog into your website using Google Tag Manager.
See our comparison of PostHog and Google Analytics 4 and An intro to PostHog for Google Analytics users for more. What's included in PostHog's free tier?
You'll never pay anything if you stay within these limits and you can set billing limits to avoid surprise bills.
A full breakdown and pricing calculator is on our pricing page . Can I use PostHog with a CDP? (Segment, Rudderstack, etc.)
Yes.

PostHog AI
Contents
* Where you can use it
* Where its data comes from
PostHog AI is an AI product analyst that lives inside PostHog. Ask it a question in plain English and it queries your data, builds the insight, writes the SQL, or finds the session replay – then explains what it found.
Because it runs on your project's own events, persons, and schema, its answers are about your product, not a generic dataset.
It also does the work, not just the analysis. PostHog AI creates dashboards, surveys, alerts, and feature flags, edits filters in the UI alongside you, and remembers what it learns about your product between conversations.
Ask it for a change that belongs in code and it starts a coding task against a repository you've connected, then reports back when there's a pull request to review.
Get started
PostHog AI lives in the PostHog web app, in a chat sidebar and in inline entry points throughout the UI. You can also talk to it in Slack, and those conversations show up in your chat history back in the web app.
PostHog Web
Chat in the sidebar, or trigger PostHog AI inline from the page you're already on.
Chat in the web app →
PostHog Slack Beta
Mention or DM @PostHog to investigate something without leaving the thread you're in.
Ask in Slack →
Where its data comes from
PostHog AI answers from your project's data, the context you attach to a conversation, and what it has saved to memory. It respects access controls , so it can only see what you can see.
Your PostHog data
Events, persons, sessions, groups, cohorts, your data warehouse schema, and every saved insight and dashboard.

Conversation context
The page you're on, plus insights, dashboards, events, and notebooks you attach to the chat yourself.
Add context →
Project memory
What your product is, who uses it, and how your team works – saved once and reused in every conversation.

evidence.title: Analyze data with PostHog AI - Docs
evidence.snippet:
Products Pricing Docs Community Company More
Get started – free
Copy page
Analyze data with PostHog AI
Contents
* How it works
* Supported insight types
* Try it
* Tips for better results
* Get started
  PostHog AI generates insights , builds dashboards , and answers questions about your product data using natural language. Describe what you want to see, and PostHog AI creates the visualization with the right events, filters, and breakdowns pre-configured.
How it works
PostHog AI identifies the right insight type (trends, funnels, retention, paths, or lifecycle), selects the relevant events and properties from your project, applies filters, breakdowns, and date ranges based on your description, and generates the visualization.
You can refine results by asking follow-up questions – like "break this down by country" or "change the date range to last 90 days" – and PostHog AI updates the insight in place.
Supported insight types
PostHog AI creates every insight type in Product Analytics:
* Insight type | What it shows
* Trends | Event counts over time
* Funnels | Conversion rates between steps
* Retention | How often users return
* Paths | How users navigate your product
* Lifecycle | New, returning, and dormant users
* Stickiness | How many days users perform an action
Beyond insights, PostHog AI can also build full dashboards , create alerts on trend metrics, and run correlation analysis to find patterns.
Try it
Select a prompt to try it out in the PostHog app:
* What changed across my product this week?
* Build a dashboard for tracking onboarding metrics
* Show me a funnel from sign up to first project created
* Which events have the highest drop-off rate in the past 7 days?
* Alert me when daily signups drop below 100
Tips for better results
* Name your events explicitly – "Show me user_signed_up events" works better than "show me signups" if PostHog AI can't match the event name
* Specify time ranges – "in the last 30 days" or "this week" helps PostHog AI scope the query correctly
* Describe the visualization you want – "as a funnel" or "broken down by browser" tells PostHog AI which insight type and breakdown to use
* Iterate with follow-ups – Ask PostHog AI to adjust filters, add breakdowns, or change the chart type after it creates the initial insight
* Ask questions, not just commands – "What changed this week?" and "Why did signups drop?" trigger PostHog AI to investigate and explain, not just build a chart

To start analyzing data with PostHog AI, set up PostHog AI .
